title: Seat races and hold expiry
idea: A seat race happens when two users check that a seat is free and both claim it; the fix makes check and claim one atomic step.

analogy.text: Two people see an empty chair, both say "free", and both sit. A chair with a lock and one key lets only one person in.
analogy.breaks: A hold's key also expires; a real key does not.

points: Check-then-act is two steps, so another thread can act in between.
A thread-safe map cannot fix it: each call is safe, the pair is not.
On a ConcurrentHashMap, `putIfAbsent` and `compute` check and write a key atomically.
Holds carry an expiry, so an abandoned checkout frees the seat by itself.

steps.caption: Unsafe version. U-7 checks whether A1 is free.
Before U-7 writes, U-9 checks too. The map is still empty.
Both threads now hold the answer yes. Neither knows about the other.
U-7 writes itself as the owner and reports success.
U-9 acts on its stale yes and overwrites the owner. Two winners, one seat.
Safe version. Both threads call `putIfAbsent` at the same moment.
The map runs one call at a time for this key. One call finds A1 empty and writes.
The other call sees an owner and returns it. That thread reports failure.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier forces both threads to look before either writes, so the race shows up every run.

walk.text: Run the same race twice: unsafe first, then atomic.
A thread-safe map, a barrier for two threads, and a winner counter.
Safe: `putIfAbsent` returns null only for the one call that wrote.
Unsafe: both check, wait for each other, then both write and win.
Join both threads before reading the count, so the output is stable.

code.title: Holds with expiry
code.caption: Time is passed in, so the expiry story replays the same way every run.

walk.text: U-7 holds A1. U-9 is refused at 18:05 but wins at 18:11.
U-7 pays late, then U-9 confirms and retries the same confirm.
A hold is expired when unbooked and its deadline has passed.
`compute` replaces the hold only if the seat is empty or expired.
Confirm with a hold id that no longer owns the seat: HOLD_LOST.
A repeated confirm is idempotent: it reports success without changing anything.
Refuse an expired hold; otherwise mark the seat booked inside the same atomic step.

pitfalls: Never check `containsKey` then `put`; use `putIfAbsent` or `compute` on the key.
If payment succeeds after HOLD_LOST, refund it; never double-assign the seat.
Lock several seats in sorted order, or two users can deadlock each other.

quiz.q: What is the first line SeatRace prints?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier makes both threads see A1 as free before either writes. Both then put and count a win: 2.

takeaway: Make check and claim one atomic step, and give every hold an expiry.

starters: Why does ConcurrentHashMap not prevent the first race?
How would I hold several seats atomically in memory?
What happens to holds if the server restarts?
